reason: E2 shows TiO precipitates form in a Ti-containing refractory HEA and contribute to high strength, but at room temperature, not 1273 K. No cited evidence addresses the thermal stability or strengthening effectiveness of TiO at 1273 K, nor the feasibility of achieving a fine dispersion in TiVNbTa specifically. The key premise of high-temperature strengthening is unsupported.
premises: TiO precipitates can form in refractory HEAs containing Ti under controlled oxygen introduction
TiO precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation motion (precipitation strengthening)
Precipitation strengthening from TiO can be effective at 1273 K
Controlled oxygen addition can produce a fine, uniform dispersion of TiO in the BCC matrix
TiO precipitation strengthening can significantly increase yield strength at 1273 K without unacceptable ductility loss
